tasks.behavior: Docs and code text keep their place on Linux and Android while the fonts load
acceptance: On Chromium for Linux, /docs at 1440 px with every font file arriving late shifts less than 0.01
notes: 2026-10-30 review fail by reviewer: Root cause confirmed in the Linux browser (pw-linux-fonts): main's fonts.ts and globals.css fail docs.spec.ts:85 at 0.0889, HEAD passes. Main's build has next/font's face 'Hanken Grotesk Fallback; src local(Arial); 99.07% / 30.02% / 0.0% / 100.94%', so the copied overrides are exact. HEAD resolves --fw-font-sans-loaded to '"Hanken Grotesk", Hanken Grotesk Fallback' and --fw-font-sans still ends in system-ui, sans-serif. Lighthouse: 98 / 100 / LCP 1862 ms. check-docs: 0 errors. Docs lines are within 25 words. The test rename names what it holds. The kit select test fails the same way on main's code in that browser (scrollbar 0), so it comes from connect mode. Defect: display optional with subsets ['latin'] preloads only the latin Hanken face. In Chromium, an optional face that starts loading after the first paint is never used in that document. Linux probe on HEAD: text added after load ('Łukasz Wiśniewski'), latin-ext face fetched in 9 ms, still 'Liberation Sans:2, Hanken Grotesk:15' for the document's life (client navigations included). Hanken only shows after a reload. On main (swap) the same probe renders all Hanken. So client-rendered names with Polish, Czech, Turkish, Romanian or Hungarian letters mix two fonts inside one word, even on a fast connection. fonts.ts, DESIGN.md and the commit say a face shows when it arrives in the short wait, which is not true for these faces. Fix tried: subsets ['latin', 'latin-ext'] makes the probe all Hanken, keeps the shift test at 3 of 3 on Linux, and Lighthouse reads 98 / 100 / LCP 1946 ms. Then say in the docs which subsets are preloaded. Note: Noto Sans (document previews) still uses next's Arial-only fallback with swap. That is the same Linux fallback bug, limited to previews. Fix it or name it.

tasks.behavior: Placeholders pulse on the compositor, so a busy page doesn't stall them
acceptance: Every placeholder's wait and pulse run on the compositor: Chromium reports no incompatible animations for them
notes: 2026-10-30 review pass by reviewer: Cause confirmed. Bare page, Chromium 156 trace: two opacity animations both report compositeFailed=64; filter pulse plus opacity fade report 0; layer count unchanged (54 vs 54 for 50 spans). 64 is 1<<6 kTargetHasIncompatibleAnimations in compositor_animations.h. filter: opacity(0.5) differs from opacity by at most 2/255 per channel (rounding); Skeleton is an empty span, so its stacking context and containing block change nothing, and opacity already made one. The reduced-motion [data-skeleton] shorthand still keeps only the fade. No other element runs two opacity animations. Kit spec passed twice, and the new test passed 8 of 8 with --repeat-each. Each row with money opens Payments at its status. Moving to wallet opens exactly the payments it sums (settlementStatus=pending). notes: 2026-10-30 review fail by subagent: Accept 1 fails: two of the three rows count money their link leaves out. A temporary balance test (since removed) showed it against a disposable DB. (1) Partially paid: a partly paid payment past its close reads state expired (ClosedSQL, R-77), but balance.go keeps it in partial (payment_status still partially_paid) until the ledger books the expiry, after the chain's finalized time passes closes_at. Test: partial +700000, list state expired. So ?state=partially_paid leaves it out, in a normal flow, for the finality lag, and that money is about to be on hold. (2) Confirming: balance.go adds every unbooked deposit, whatever the payment's state: an extra deposit on a paid payment, a late one after close, one on a non-chosen option, one on an expired or canceled payment. PaymentStateSQL reads those payments as paid, overpaid, expired or canceled, and ConfirmingSQL needs block_time <= closes_at on the shown option. Test: confirming +200000, list state paid. Moving is right: settlement_status=pending is set only when the option becomes paid, and the settle outflow that sets settled takes its payable; delayed and refused are included. Fix: in balance.go, sort pending into parts by the list's own predicates (no closed partials, no off-state unbooked deposits), update R-33 and TestPendingParts; or stop claiming each row opens exactly the payments it counts. Minor: with prices failed, a zero part reads '—' and is a link; link names have no 'USD'; DESIGN.md line 179 still lists only Moving to wallet and Not final; a Finance member limited to some stores sees the whole profile's totals but only their stores' list; when linkId and settlementStatus are both set there are two 'Show all payments' buttons; BUSINESS_COPY.open was already unused before this change.
